Hi Dylan / Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to formalize the MAP and surface the unit economics assumptions so finance can sign off before we commit to a pilot. Two quick asks to start the MAP:

1) A short table of tokens-per-request assumptions for our 3 main flows (summary note, chart ingestion, conversational Q&A).
2) Expected caching hit-rate assumptions (prefix + KV) and whether Redwood will provide prefetch/persistent warming for the pilot.
3) Recommended batching window (ms) and expected tokens/$ at the pilot throughput (we can target ~50 req/s average for the PoC).

I've attached a draft MAP that includes a placeholder cost model — it's intentionally conservative. Can you review and send a version with your econ rows filled? Procurement wants the final MAP + PO pathway captured by next Friday so finance can review.

Attachments: [MAP_draft_v0.3.xlsx (xlsx)]

Best,
Samantha Lee

Samantha.lee@asterhealth.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: units per $ reconciliation and pilot cadence

Samantha — thanks, and really appreciate the clear asks. We're happy to own the econ rows and lock down a short validation sprint. High-level answers below; I'll follow-up with an updated MAP spreadsheet by EOD with the rows filled and a proposed 2-week sprint plan.

Quick answers:
- Tokens per request (ballpark):
  * Summarization (avg user doc 800 tokens in / 120 tokens out): ~920 tokens/request
  * Chart ingestion (OCR + embedding + indexing): ~2,400 tokens/request
  * Conversational Q&A (context window ~3k tokens, avg generation ~220): ~3,220 tokens/request

- Caching: we recommend prefix caching for FAQ-style queries (expected hit-rate 40–60% depending on prompt normalization). KV cache helps reduce decoder tokens for multi-turn sessions — expect 15–25% savings on gen tokens for sessions with repeated context. We will enable prefix caching for the pilot and provide a warmup script.

- Batching: default batching window 50ms yields good latency/cost balance on dedicated pools; at 50 req/s we expect continuous batching to net ~1.6–2.2x tokens/$ improvement versus single-request baseline depending on model selection and sequence lengths.

I'll attach the updated MAP + a short evaluation plan with stepwise acceptance criteria (quality thresholds, latency budget, token accounting checks). Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize econ rows and mutual action plan (this thread)
- Week 1: pilot setup + warmup; run initial baseline sims and live trace capture
- Week 2: run cost-sensitivity sims and quality evals; decision checkpoint for PO/scale

Can we schedule a 30-min alignment call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT?

Attachments: [redwood-econ-assumptions.pdf (pdf), MAP_draft_v0.3.xlsx (updated)]

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 13:40:05 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: units per $ reconciliation and pilot cadence

Adding technical detail from the ops side so the pilot simulation is realistic.

- Model baseline: recommend gpt-small-open-quant (8-bit) for pilot to hit cost targets while keeping latency < 200ms p95 with our dedicated pool.
- Batching behavior: with a 50ms aggregation window and continuous batching we'll typically get batches of 6–10 requests at 50 RPS sustained — that drives the 1.6–2.2x cost improvement Dylan referenced. If peak bursts are higher (>200 RPS) we fall back to smaller batch sizes and the delta tightens.
- Prefetch/warmup: we'll run a prefix-warmup job to populate KV caches; expect warmup to reduce early pilot cost by ~10–12% over the first 24 hours.
- Instrumentation: we'll create a token accounting dashboard (tokens/request, cache hits, batching factor) that updates in near real-time and share a view with Aster.

I'll update the MAP econ sheet with these operational assumptions and a short methodology note for how we measured the batch factor in simulation.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: MAP + Evaluation plan (deliverables & acceptance criteria)

Samantha — attaching the edited MAP and a concise evaluation plan — pulled the econ rows together and added acceptance criteria so finance, procurement, and engineering have clear signoff gates. Key points below; full details are in the evaluation-plan.md.

Summary (high level):
- Units per $ table: populated with per-flow tokens, expected batching factor, expected cache hit-rate, and derived tokens-per-dollar at pilot throughput (50 RPS). See sheet 'econ-summary'.
- Acceptance criteria (must meet all):
  1) Token accounting traceable: token-level logs for 100% of pilot requests (audit sample 1k requests)
  2) Cost per 1k requests within 12% of model projection after warmup phase
  3) p95 latency <= 250ms for the conversational flow during 95th percentile traffic window
  4) Cache hit-rate >= 35% on normalized FAQ queries after warmup
  5) No data egress exceptions — all logs stored per Aster retention policy (30d)

Deliverables & owners:
- Redwood: updated MAP spreadsheet (attached), warmup script, token accounting dashboard link, cost-sensitivity sims (cost-sensitivity-sims.csv) — owner: Ben
- Aster: share representative traffic samples and black-box QoE prompts — owner: Samantha

Timeline (compressed):
- Thu (today): sign MAP econ rows
- Fri (tomorrow): Redwood sends warmup script + baseline sims
- Week 1 (pilot week): run pilot and gather traces; mid-week checkpoint meeting
- Week 2: run sims, finalize PO decision by EOW if acceptance criteria met

Attachments: [evaluation-plan.md, cost-sensitivity-sims.csv, MAP_draft_v0.3.xlsx (final econ rows)]

Please confirm and I'll draft a short mutual action plan with explicit PO/POC milestones and acceptance signoff columns.
